findings.claim: Decoded terminal learning labels are unavailable (decoded_terminal_learning_labels_available=false). Descendant credit in lineage_support is recorded joint-head credit over the learning window [0.0,0.5] with terminal score time 0.99, not decoded terminal affinity. Therefore last-record survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit; the immediate-selection versus descendant-credit comparison is unavailable.

Survival enrichment is weak and mostly null: landmark_00_soft_mass (survival_effects:0, z=0.365, q=0.120), landmark_07_soft_mass (survival_effects:70, z=0.220, q=0.356), landmark_10_soft_mass (survival_effects:100, z=0.234, q=0.302), landmark_18_local_czz (survival_effects:186, z=0.217, q=0.302). Only landmark_02_local_dz (survival_effects:23, z=0.206, q=0.356) and landmark_04_local_czz (survival_effects:46, z=0.266, q=0.302) reach nominal significance, and none survive BH at q<0.05. Survival credit does not identify a robust coordinate direction.

Immediate endpoint selection evidence is strong for pair_kernel_1.5 (endpoint_effects:9, integrated z=0.562, q=1.5e-4, positive batch fraction 1.0), pair_kernel_2.5 (endpoint_effects:10, z=0.631, q=2.2e-5, fraction 1.0), pair_kernel_3.5 (endpoint_effects:11, z=0.540, q=9.8e-5, fraction 1.0), pair_kernel_5.0 (endpoint_effects:12, z=0.319, q=0.0037), landmark_00_occupancy3 (endpoint_effects:15, z=0.545, q=2.4e-4, fraction 1.0), and negative for pair_kernel_7.0 (endpoint_effects:13, z=-0.485, q=1.5e-4, fraction 0.0), shape_yy (endpoint_effects:4, z=-0.513, q=1.5e-5, fraction 0.0), shape_xx (endpoint_effects:3, z=-0.495, q=8.1e-4). This is the strongest available direction evidence, but it is selection evidence, not decoded terminal affinity benefit.

Branch-adjusted covariance and correlation agree with the endpoint direction for pair_kernel_1.5 (branch_adjusted:86, q=0.081; branch_adjusted:240, q=0.019, same-sign batch fraction 0.929) and pair_kernel_2.5 (branch_adjusted:87, q=0.077; branch_adjusted:241, q=0.046, fraction 0.929), and for shape_yy negative (branch_adjusted:235, q=1.5e-2, fraction 1.0; branch_adjusted:158, q=2.6e-3, fraction 1.0). Joint diagnostics are strongly negative: joint_innovation_RMS_A (branch_adjusted:305, q=2.8e-4, fraction 0.929; branch_adjusted:228, q=9.3e-5, fraction 1.0) and joint_internal_RMS_A (branch_adjusted:307, q=9.7e-4, fraction 1.0; branch_adjusted:230, q=1.5e-4, fraction 1.0).

Global centroid coordinates do not survive adjustment: raw_covariance global_centroid_x/y/z (branch_adjusted:0,1,2) have q=0.72, 0.69, 0.97 and same-sign batch fractions 0.50, 0.43, 0.36; adjusted_covariance (branch_adjusted:77,78,79) q=0.97, 0.86, 0.91; adjusted_correlation (branch_adjusted:231,232,233) q=0.81, 0.74, 0.53. Centroid motion is not a reproducible coordinate direction.

Joint pose diagnostics separate global motion from internal structure: joint_translation_RMS_A is weaker (branch_adjusted:75, q=0.095; branch_adjusted:152, q=0.072; branch_adjusted:229, q=0.087; branch_adjusted:306, q=0.052) than joint_internal_RMS_A (branch_adjusted:76, q=0.044; branch_adjusted:153, q=0.030; branch_adjusted:230, q=1.5e-4; branch_adjusted:307, q=9.7e-4) and joint_innovation_RMS_A (branch_adjusted:74, q=0.038; branch_adjusted:151, q=0.020; branch_adjusted:228, q=9.3e-5; branch_adjusted:305, q=2.8e-4). Internal and innovation RMS carry the reproducible signal; translation does not.

Within-selector joint diagnostics show selection innovation is negatively associated with observed child score gain (joint_diagnostics:2, mean -0.036, p=1.8e-7, positive batch fraction 0.0), while positively associated with innovation_native_alignment (joint_diagnostics:1, mean 0.092, p=1.5e-9) and teacher_innovation_contrast_alignment (joint_diagnostics:11, mean 0.226, p=1.2e-9). Teacher contrast is predominantly internal (joint_diagnostics:14, mean 0.787) rather than translation (joint_diagnostics:12, mean 0.132) or rotation (joint_diagnostics:13, mean 0.081). These are descriptive within-selector associations, not causal affinity effects.

Continuous contrast functions for landmark_00 are observed-node linear interpolations over support [0.0,0.49] with extrapolation_allowed=false and polynomial_accepted=false. They show many sign changes (e.g., continuous:1 landmark_00_local_dx has 6 sign changes and 9 strong sign conflicts; continuous:7 landmark_00_local_cxy has 9 sign changes and 14 strong sign conflicts) and high relative node RMSE (0.28-0.87). A constant rule is not supported; a time-conditioned rule would require validated fits that are not accepted here.

Soft-mass contrast curves across landmarks are non-monotone with multiple sign changes and no accepted polynomial fit (e.g., continuous:0 landmark_00_soft_mass degree 3, 4 sign changes, relative node RMSE 0.286; continuous:10 landmark_01_soft_mass 4 sign changes, RMSE 0.622; continuous:90 landmark_09_soft_mass 10 sign changes, RMSE 0.806). The curves are not absolute reward targets and do not establish a causal benefit or gradient.

Curve fidelity audit selected 24 curves under the rule relative_rmse_le=0.35, strong_sign_conflict_nodes_eq=0, quiet_node_large_fit_fraction_le=0.1, absolute_integrated_z_ge=0.1, batch_direction_fraction_ge=0.857, q_lt=0.05. The audit reports legendre_runtime_allowed=false for all listed curves and last_empirical_z versus last_fit_z sign disagreements (e.g., landmark_00_occupancy3 last_empirical_z=-0.040 vs last_fit_z=0.545; landmark_16_occupancy5 last_empirical_z=0.315 vs last_fit_z=-0.175 with 15 strong sign conflict nodes). Fits are not validated for runtime use.

Turnover accounting separates population rate, edge rate, and turnover residual. For landmark_00_soft_mass, population_rate z=0.185 (turnover:0, p=0.72) while edge_rate z=4.545 (turnover:1, p=0.034) and turnover_residual_rate z=-4.360 (turnover:2, p=0.034). Large positive residuals appear for landmark_00_local_cxx (turnover:14, z=4.286, p=0.002), landmark_00_local_cyy (turnover:17, z=5.051, p=0.0015), landmark_01_local_cyy (turnover:47, z=6.397, p=4.3e-4), landmark_04_local_cxx (turnover:134, z=5.671, p=2.5e-5), landmark_07_local_cxx (turnover:224, z=5.076, p=1.1e-4), landmark_07_local_cyy (turnover:227, z=5.633, p=6.3e-4), landmark_16_local_cyy (turnover:497, z=6.367, p=1.2e-4), and landmark_19_local_cyy (turnover:587, z=5.368, p=0.0012). The residual is an accounting diagnostic including reclassification and parent weighting, not a causal selection effect or atom velocity.

Parent-child increment contrasts are mostly null or weak: landmark_00_softmin (increment_effects:14, q=0.046, rate z=-4.914, positive batch fraction 0.071) and landmark_00_occupancy3 (increment_effects:15, q=0.081, z=4.277, fraction 0.857) are the strongest; shape_xx (increment_effects:3, q=0.095, z=-3.698), shape_yy (increment_effects:4, q=0.161, z=-3.845), shape_xz (increment_effects:7, q=0.207, z=3.004), pair_kernel_2.5 (increment_effects:10, q=0.208, z=3.965), pair_kernel_7.0 (increment_effects:13, q=0.208, z=-3.139). These increment contrasts do not establish within-path change versus changing cohort composition.

hypotheses.claim: A coordinate intervention on pair-distance shell density at a=1.5-2.5 A (pair_kernel_1.5, pair_kernel_2.5) is the best-supported testable hypothesis: observable is the pair_kernel contrast, intended response is increased favorable-minus-comparison contrast, target origin is the endpoint pointcloud reward, spatial scale is 1.5-2.5 A pair distance, and a discriminating failure condition is loss of the positive batch fraction (currently 1.0 at endpoint and 0.929 at branch-adjusted) or reversal of the integrated z sign.

A joint internal-motion hypothesis: reducing joint_internal_RMS_A and joint_innovation_RMS_A while preserving internal (non-translation) teacher contrast is testable via the endpoint pointcloud reward. Observable is joint_internal_RMS_A and joint_innovation_RMS_A; intended response is reduced internal RMS; target origin is the endpoint pointcloud reward; spatial scale is whole-molecule internal geometry; discriminating failure is unchanged or increased internal RMS with no change in observed child score gain.

A shape_yy reduction hypothesis: observable is shape_yy (negative endpoint effect, q=1.5e-5, positive batch fraction 0.0; branch-adjusted q=1.5e-2, fraction 1.0), intended response is reduced shape_yy, target origin is the endpoint pointcloud reward, spatial scale is global shape anisotropy, discriminating failure is a sign reversal or loss of the zero positive batch fraction.

A time-conditioned regional attention hypothesis is not currently expressible: the supplied continuous contrast curves have no accepted polynomial fit, extrapolation_allowed=false, and legendre_runtime_allowed=false, so a time-conditioned rule cannot be validated from the supplied evidence. It remains descriptive until validated fits or observed-node interpolation within support are available.

A within-path change versus cohort-composition hypothesis: the large positive turnover residuals for local_cxx and local_cyy at landmarks 00, 01, 04, 07, 16, 19 could reflect reclassification or parent weighting rather than within-path coordinate change. Discriminating evidence would be a parent-debiased increment contrast that retains the same sign and magnitude; the supplied increment contrasts are mostly null, so the hypothesis remains unresolved.

A teacher-alignment hypothesis: compressed choice excess fixed RMS is 0.081 A (CI 0.070-0.092) and top4 teacher overlap is 0.470 (CI 0.427-0.515), with chosen teacher score correlation 0.102 (CI 0.065-0.140). This is observational and not a fitted or independently validated affinity predictor; it does not establish neural-module causation or physical interaction energy.

limitations: Descendant credit is recorded joint-head credit, not decoded terminal affinity; decoded terminal learning labels are unavailable.
Turnover residual includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, not only resampling.
Adjusted branch covariance is supplied evidence; region moments themselves are not rigid-motion residuals.
Curve fitting does not establish causal benefit or a gradient; no time bins or outside-window analysis.
Static teachers are last-learning-node forecasts, not actual final structures.
All weak and null scalar effects retained; current study outcomes are withheld from design roles.
Moment effects, pair kernels and turnover rates are diagnostic evidence only; the executing pointcloud scalar has no pair-kernel, moment, joint-motif or geometry-block term.
Temperatures are immutable task parameters; no temperature edit is proposed.
